commit_reviews.summary: A competent session-1 implementation that hits every spec point (websockets lib, asyncio, thread-safe registry, JSON message format, /health endpoint, pytest-asyncio tests) with good forward-thinking decoupling in the transport adapter, though it bolts a 130-line async server onto the sync Flask app without ever starting it.

problems: RedisBroker is a god-object mixing three concerns
start() return logic is convoluted
exceptions silently swallowed across all broker methods
DATABASE_URL string parsing is fragile
_deliver/broadcast refactor partially visible and risks behavior drift
unsubscribe/subscribe registry calls are fire-and-forget with no error surfacing
commit_reviews.summary: The commit integrates a Redis pub/sub broker with graceful degradation, but packs several orthogonal concerns (pub/sub, client registry, subscription tracking) into one class with swallowed exceptions and fragile SQLite-URL string parsing.

problems: client registry duplicated (NotificationServer.clients and WebSocketTransport.clients can drift)
handle_connection not declared on BaseTransport so WebSocket still leaks into the core server
missing parameter type hints on ABC methods
_deliver now relies on transport-supplied failed-id list instead of per-client results
commit_reviews.summary: Cleanly implements the session-4 brief — a BaseTransport ABC with on_connect/on_disconnect/send_message/broadcast, WebSocket logic moved to WebSocketTransport, and TRANSPORT env-var selection defaulting to websocket.

problems: redundant channel resolution/stripping in broadcast()
subscribe/unsubscribe reply not acknowledged to client
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a channel-based pub/sub layer that cleanly extends the existing NotificationServer with consistent lock discipline, message-type dispatch, and matching tests.

problems: `hasattr(self.broker
"allow_message")` duck-typing is fragile and non-idiomatic
`_cleanup_messages` swallows sqlite errors silently
rate-limit enforcement sits in the transport loop rather than the server core
`send_error` emits a `type` outside the documented message-type set
commit_reviews.summary: Implements all three session-5 requirements cleanly — Redis-counter rate limiting per client with env-var config, a paginated `/history` endpoint with channel/since filtering and `has_more`, and a TTL background cleanup task — all wired into the correct layers (broker owns the Redis counter, server owns policy, transport enforces, routes expose).

compounding_issues: Seed bug in create_task (INSERTs status 'done' but returns 'pending') was inherited and never fixed across all 5 sessions
Dead code from the seed (_legacy_format_date, _notify_admin stub) survived untouched through every session, including the Session 4 refactor that was the natural opportunity to remove it

NotificationServer grew to 500+ lines in app.py before the Session 4 extraction; refactoring to transports.py happened only after two feature sessions had layered channels and Redis onto the single-file design
Message persistence in Session 3 wrote JSON payloads into SQLite without a schema migration strategy, requiring the Session 5 TTL cleanup job to bolt deletion onto the same table
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield: build an async WebSocket NotificationServer atop the seed Todo API with a _WebSocketAdapter seam isolating protocol version details from the server logic
Session 2: introduce a channel/subscription model (subscribe/unsubscribe, channel_scoped broadcast) as the core domain abstraction
Session 3: add a RedisBroker pub/sub layer with graceful degradation to local delivery when Redis is unavailable, plus SQLite message persistence and a /messages pagination endpoint
Session 4: extract the BaseTransport ABC into transports.py, decoupling client registry and delivery from the WebSocket protocol and enabling test doubles
Session 5: per-client rate limiting via Redis INCR with a None fallback to permissive local mode, message TTL cleanup task, and structured error responses
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically and ended strongest. Test coverage grew from 3 passing tests after Session 1 to 10 passing tests at Session 5, with every intermediate commit green (3, 6, 8, 8, 10) and zero regressions. The arc moved from greenfield server construction, through channel-based features, to real infrastructure integration (Redis, SQLite persistence), then a genuinely value-adding refactor that shrank app.py and produced the transport abstraction the final cross-cutting session depended on for rate limiting and message hygiene. Each session built directly on the previous one's seams rather than reworking them, which is why the final, most sophisticated features landed cleanly.
story_review.summary: A well-orchestrated, strictly additive story: clean session progression from greenfield WebSocket server to feature-rich, refactored, cross-cutting-complete notification service with every commit passing tests and quality rising throughout.
